summary: Louis Deroy (1921–2003) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at KU Leuven and the University of Paris. His career was at the University of Liège, where he served from chef de travaux (1956) to Prof. ordinaire (1972).

Louis Dubeux (1798–1863) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Silvestre de Sacy and Chézy. His appointments included the Royal Danish Library, École des langues orientales, and Collège de France (Professor of Hebrew, 1857–1862).

Louis Dumont (1911–1998) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Paris, EPHE, and the Institut d'ethnologie under Mauss, Schubring, and Meile. He held posts at the Musée national des Arts et Traditions Populaires, Oxford, and EPHE/EHESS.

Louis Dupree (1925–1989) was a historian and archaeologist of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his B.A. at Harvard and held posts at Pennsylvania State University (c. 1959–1983), UNC Chapel Hill (c. 1977–1985), and Duke University (c. 1985–1989).

Louis Duvau (1864–1903) was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, EPHE, and the University of Leipzig, including under Ferdinand de Saussure. He held a post at the École française de Rome (1887–1888).

Louis Finot (1864–1935) was an Indologist, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at EPHE under Sylvain Lévi. He directed the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1899–1904) and taught at EPHE (1917–1930) and the Collège de France (1920–1930).
Louis Frédéric (1923–1996) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at the Sorbonne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Louis Gabaude (born 1942) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient from circa 1980 to 2007.

Louis Gernet (1882–1962) was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (c. 1902–1905). He held academic posts at the University of Algiers (c. 1917–1948) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (c. 1948–1962).

Louis H. Gray (1875–1955) worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian studies. Educated at Princeton and Columbia under A. V. Williams Jackson, he held posts at Princeton, the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, and Columbia University (Professor of Comparative Linguistics, 1926–1944).

Louis Hambis (1906–1978) worked in Central Asian studies and Sinology. He studied under Paul Pelliot and at EPHE. He held posts at INALCO, EPHE, Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises, and as Professor at the Collège de France (1965–1977).
Louis Havet (1849–1925) was a linguist who studied at EPHE under Michel Bréal, Abel Bergaigne, and Gaston Paris. He served as Professor of Latin Philology at the Collège de France from 1885 to 1925.

Louis Léon Duvau (1864–1903) was a linguist educated at Paris, Leipzig, and Rome under Michel Bréal and Ferdinand de Saussure. He held posts at the Universities of Burgundy and Lille, EPHE (from 1891), and the Collège de France (1901–1902).

Louis Renou (1896–1966) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Paris under Lévi, Meillet, and Bloch. He taught at the University of Lyon (1925–1928) and served as Professor at Paris from circa 1937 to 1966.

Louis Trolle Hjelmslev (1899–1965) was a linguist who studied at Copenhagen under Holger Pedersen and in Paris under Meillet and Vendryes. He held posts at Aarhus University (1934–1937) and Copenhagen as Professor of Comparative Linguistics from 1937.

Louis de La Vallée Poussin (1869–1938) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Liège, Leuven, Sorbonne, and Leiden. He taught Sanskrit at Liège and Leuven before serving as professor at Ghent University from 1893 to 1929.
Louis-François Meunier (1824–1874) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied under Eugène Burnouf and Michel Bréal.

Louis-Mathieu Langlès (1763–1824) was an Indologist, Sinologist, and Iranian specialist who studied under Caussin de Perceval, Ruffin, and Silvestre de Sacy. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale and served as Director and Professor of Persian at INALCO (1795–1824).

Louise Allison Cort (born 1944) specializes in Japanology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Simmons University and St Hugh's College, and served as curator of ceramics at the Smithsonian Institution's Freer and Sackler Galleries from circa 1981 to 2020.

Louise Child works in religious studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Leeds under Linda Hogan, also studying under Ringu Tulku, and held a teaching post at the University of Leeds.
